title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

reading.body:
This is an access-control failure inside a legitimate law enforcement tool. A camera network built to support police work was queried by an officer for a purpose unrelated to any case, and the same officer is accused of running the same searches through other restricted databases. The failure sits at the point of use, not at the point of design: the system performed the lookups it was asked to perform.

What would have caught it is a check on who is asking and why. The reporting does not describe any audit, alert, or approval step that flagged the searches while they were happening, and it does not say whether the systems logged them in a way anyone reviewed. Detection here depended on the woman recognising what had happened to her, not on the systems themselves.

The accusation is that a person with authorised access used that access against someone he knew. It is not established that Rogers committed a crime, that the searches violated state law, or that the department failed in any duty. A complaint, an internal investigation, and a leave decision are not findings of guilt, and the employment question is still before the town.

reports.title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

summary:
A Stow police officer, Jason Rogers, is accused of misusing police databases to track a woman he previously dated. The woman said she ended the abusive relationship about five years ago and changed her identity, phone number, and social media habits. She discovered this summer that Rogers had searched for her location using the Flock camera system and other law enforcement databases, including CJIS and CORI, multiple times in 2024 and 2025. She also said he drove by her home.

The Stow Police Department filed a criminal complaint against Rogers on July 17 for possible state law violations. After a four-week internal affairs investigation, the department placed him on paid administrative leave in July, then unpaid leave as of July 31. The woman has obtained a restraining order lasting at least a year. A Select Board hearing is scheduled next week, when town leaders could vote on Rogers' employment status.
